name: bluewater-25-ice
lines: In eighteen oh six, a twenty two year old from Boston loaded a ship with ice. And sailed it to the Caribbean.
The newspapers laughed at him. Then he lost his money. Then he went to prison.
And then he built a fortune out of frozen water.
His name was Frederic Tudor. They called him the Ice King.
Here is his story. And four moves you can use this week.
Boston. Every winter, the ponds freeze solid. The ice is free. And nobody wants it.
Two thousand miles south, it is hot all year. And nobody there has ever had a cold drink.
Tudor looks at those two facts. And sees a business.
Cut the ice here. Sell it there.
He asks ship owners to carry it. Every one of them says no.
So he buys his own ship.
In February he sails for the island of Martinique. With a hundred and thirty tons of pond ice.
A Boston paper prints the news. We hope this will not prove a slippery speculation.
Weeks later, he lands. And much of the ice has made it.
Then he hits a problem he never thought about.
Nobody on the island knows what ice is for. And there is nowhere to keep it.
It melts on the dock. He loses thousands.
Move one. Nobody buys what they do not understand.
Tudor had a great product. And customers with no idea why they would want it.
So he goes back. And this time he does not start by selling. He starts by teaching.
He walks into bars. And he gives the barkeeper ice. Free.
He shows him how to keep it. And how to chill a drink with it.
So a cold drink costs the customer the same as a warm one.
He wrote down why. A man who has his drinks cold for one week can never be given them warm again.
He was right. People tried it once. And never went back.
Move two. Let them try it first.
But the business still bleeds. Ice melts on every trip. Cargo after cargo, lost.
The debts pile up. In eighteen twelve, they put him in debtors prison.
In his journal he writes, let those laugh who win.
He gets out. And he goes straight back to the ice.
He tests everything. Straw. Wood shavings. Rice husks.
Then the one that works. Sawdust. The sawmills throw it away.
And he builds ice houses in the ports. So the ice lasts.
Move three. Fix what happens after the sale.
Now for the trip everyone said could not be done.
Eighteen thirty three. One hundred and eighty tons of ice. Boston to Calcutta, in India.
Four months at sea. Across the equator. Twice.
When the ship comes in, about a hundred tons are still frozen.
The city goes wild. People who have never seen ice hold it in their hands.
Move four. Keep going. It took twenty seven years to get from that first ship to this one.
So here are the four. One. If they do not understand it, they will not buy it. Teach first.
Two. Let them try it. A taste beats any promise.
Three. Look after it once it is sold. That is where the money leaks.
And four. The people who laughed gave up. He did not.
Your business. Our marketing department. Bluewater Co.
